head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: Blacklist and duplicate checks are case-sensitive and the server never rejects duplicate guests.
reason: The schema is only `z.array(z.string().email())` with no lowercasing or uniqueness rule, and line 77 compares the raw `guest` against the lowercased blacklist with `includes`, so mixed-case emails and duplicates in one request reach `createMany`.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: Emails are sent using the raw `guests` input instead of the filtered `uniqueGuests`.
reason: `sendAddGuestsEmails` (email-manager.ts:541) sends `AttendeeScheduledEmail` to every attendee in `newGuests`, and line 168 passes the unfiltered `guests`, so an existing attendee who is re-submitted gets a confirmation email.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: Admin/owner check uses && so team admins who are not owners are denied.
reason: `isTeamAdmin` matches role ADMIN or OWNER, so `isTeamAdmin && isTeamOwner` at lines 46-48 only lets owners through and rejects plain admins.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the organizer's, and a failure here is not caught.
reason: Lines 158-163 build `EventManager` from `ctx.user`'s credentials, not the organizer's (`booking.user`), and `updateCalendarAttendees` at line 165 has no try/catch after the attendees were already written.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: The fallback error message can never be shown.
reason: The template string at line 43 is never empty, so `t("unable_to_add_guests")` can never be shown, and `isInvalidEmail` is only reset by the Cancel button.

head: 92f44dcea7ff19e9123a30c63c167a2938df5a55
title: Any attendee can add unlimited arbitrary emails, which then get mail sent in the organizer's name.
reason: The handler explicitly checks `isAttendee` at line 52 to let attendees add guests, so attendee access is a deliberate product choice, not a defect.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Accessing `.integration` on a possibly undefined destination calendar crashes booking creation.
reason: Line 118 yields undefined when destinationCalendar is null, and line 119 reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without `?.` for Meet locations, which throws.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: The slug condition is inverted for organization creation.
reason: The diff replaces `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` with `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`, inverting when the slug is set.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: The delete fallback never matches, so deletes always target "primary".
reason: Lines 315-317 run `find` only when externalCalendarId is falsy and compare against that falsy value, so it never matches and the delete falls back to 'primary' instead of the old destinationCalendar.externalId.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Video references no longer store a credentialId.
reason: Line 170 now stores `credentialId: undefined` for video results (it used to store result.credentialId), and handleCancelBooking line 491 depends on bookingVideoReference.credentialId.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Collective hosts' calendars are dropped when the organizer has no destination calendar.
reason: Lines 1063-1067 fall back to null, so `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars)` at line 1078 does nothing and the other hosts' calendars are dropped.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Destination calendars without a credentialId now get events in "primary" instead of the selected calendar.
reason: EventManager's no-credentialId branch calls createEvent(c, event), and the Google service selects by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`, which never matches a null credentialId, so the event goes to 'primary' where the old code used the destination's externalId.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: updateLocation references lose externalCalendarId.
reason: CalendarManager.updateEvent (lines 313-322) returns neither externalId nor credentialId, so updateLocation's references at lines 208-209 get externalCalendarId undefined.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: Recurring cancellation repeats once per reference but only deletes the first calendar reference of each booking.
reason: The recurring branch at lines 449-461 sits inside the per-reference loop but deletes only `updBooking.references.find(...)`, the first calendar reference, repeating the same delete and never removing the other hosts' events.

head: de628295646d0848226618108a52f2f1e5d04ac0
title: The loadUsers rewrite drops the organization select and changes error behaviour.
reason: Nothing in handleNewBooking.ts reads organizerUser.organization; getBookerUrl uses only organizationId, so removing the organization select has no effect, and the error-handling point is a minor remark.

head: da09bc0808e7c6df1bc10e00d5acf764d94c7cc7
title: The "Caching" tests were deleted instead of updated.
reason: Removing the caching tests only reduces test coverage: the caching code at insightsBooking.ts:84-92 is unchanged, and the author removed the tests on purpose in the 'clean up tests' commit.

head: da09bc0808e7c6df1bc10e00d5acf764d94c7cc7
title: The new public options type no longer catches a team scope without `teamId` at compile time.
reason: The only code that creates InsightsBookingService is the integration test, and every call passes valid options, so no caller can hit the missing-teamId case; this is a type-strictness remark.

head: da09bc0808e7c6df1bc10e00d5acf764d94c7cc7
title: Removing the public `findMany` method can break existing callers.
reason: A search for InsightsBookingService finds nothing outside the service and its own test, so no findMany caller exists to break.

head: 6048e2a86b50e81e1e3b1b467dfea5a895add3dc
title: Reschedules still cancel at SendGrid immediately, so they still count toward the 100-cancellation limit.
reason: handleNewBooking.ts:968 passes immediateDelete=true, which POSTs status:cancel to SendGrid immediately (emailReminderManager.ts:213-222), so reschedules still hit the 100-pending-cancel limit the PR says is the cause, and the row is never flagged for cron retry.

head: 6048e2a86b50e81e1e3b1b467dfea5a895add3dc
title: A cancellation made shortly before the send time is never cancelled at SendGrid.
reason: emailReminderManager.ts:225-232 only sets cancelled:true and the cron runs every 15 minutes, so a reminder cancelled within ~15 minutes of its send time can be sent before the cron cancels it.

head: 6048e2a86b50e81e1e3b1b467dfea5a895add3dc
title: One failed SendGrid cancel stops the whole batch and can leave the cron stuck on that reminder.
reason: scheduleEmailReminders.ts:53-77 wraps the whole loop in one try, so a single client.request throw skips later reminders and the lazy prisma deletes behind Promise.all at line 74 never run.

head: 6048e2a86b50e81e1e3b1b467dfea5a895add3dc
title: Reminder database writes are now fire-and-forget instead of awaited.
reason: bookings.tsx:488-494 now calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder without awaiting, while the old code awaited Promise.all on the DB deletes, so the cancelled:true write is fire-and-forget.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: Busy times are skipped on any day that has a date override.
reason: Lines 133-135 `if (dateOverrideExist) return true;` exit before `busy.every(...)`, so bookings and calendar events are never checked on days with an override.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: Any working-hours range that doesn't contain the slot rejects it, so a day with several ranges loses slots.
reason: The `workingHours.find` at lines 138-148 returns true (unavailable) when any range on that day excludes the slot, so a day with split ranges rejects slots that another range contains.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: The date-override bounds checks compare by reference and ignore slots that run past the override's end.
reason: Line 114 compares two new dayjs objects with `===`, which is always false, and line 123 only checks `slotStartTime.isAfter(end)`, so slots that run past the override's end are accepted.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: The working-hours end check uses the slot's start time instead of its end time.
reason: Line 142 computes `end` from `slotStartTime`, so a slot that runs past the end of working hours is not caught.

head: ee38fd295fd294b9fc787eba482bde24bbfea69b
title: Shifting the override by the timezone offset can wrap past midnight, giving an endTime earlier than startTime.
reason: Lines 218-223 shift the start and end by the offset and then keep only hour*60+minute, so a 20:00-23:00 override shifted by +2h becomes start 1320, end 60, an inverted range.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Migration crashes when no embed_category row matches a category.
reason: Lines 9-15 index `[0]` on a PG::Result with no row check; when embed_category was never set the join returns no rows and PG raises IndexError, aborting the migration.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Existing hosts are copied unnormalized and interpolated straight into SQL.
reason: Line 25 inserts raw split values without normalization or quoting, while record_for_host compares against uri.host, so migrated hosts like 'http://discourse.org' never match.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: update/destroy raise NoMethodError on an unknown id.
reason: `EmbeddableHost.where(id: params[:id]).first` can be nil, and `save_host(nil)` or `nil.destroy` then raises a 500 instead of a 404.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: before_validation crashes when host is nil.
reason: `self.host.sub!` in before_validation raises NoMethodError when host is nil, e.g. a create request without embeddable_host[:host].

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Host lookup fails for mixed-case referers and for hosts saved with a port.
reason: Line 17 lowercases only the column, not uri.host, which keeps its case; the validation also allows a port that is never stripped, and uri.host never includes one.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Irreversible deletion of site settings inside a reversible `change`.
reason: Inside a Rails `change` migration, `execute` is irreversible, so rollback raises IrreversibleMigration rather than silently losing the settings as claimed.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: Plural `_ids` hydration crashes on null and keeps unresolved entries.
reason: The only `_ids` key in the rest_serializer payloads is embeddable_host_ids from a has_many with embed: :ids, which is always an array, so the null case cannot happen here.

head: d1c69189f3c90ecf56013a8da904da9bff9a8e19
title: expandable_first_post? no longer depends on any embeddable host existing.
reason: The embeddable_hosts site setting was deliberately removed by this PR, so dropping that check is an intended change, not a defect.

head: 5f8a130277dbddc95d133cd2832be639baf89213
title: Blocked-email lookup is case-sensitive, so changing the letter case gets past the block.
reason: `BlockedEmail.where(email: email)` is an exact match, and nothing on the path lowercases the address: User sets `user.email = params[:email]` with no downcase, and `Email.downcase` (lib/email.rb:21) only lowercases the domain anyway, so changing the case of the local part gets past the block.

head: 5f8a130277dbddc95d133cd2832be639baf89213
title: A rejected email always shows the generic 'invalid' message, whatever the server's reason was.
reason: The server's own message is already flashed (`flash(result.message ...)`), so the user sees the real reason; the generic inline 'invalid' text is a wording remark, not a defect.

head: 5f8a130277dbddc95d133cd2832be639baf89213
title: The match_count increment can lose updates when signups overlap.
reason: Lines 14-16 read the count, add one in Ruby and save it back, so two overlapping signups for the same blocked email can lose an increment; it is a narrow race, but a real one.

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: The light-theme value for post author links changes from 30% to 70% lightness, and the pair is reversed.
reason: In desktop/topic-post.scss line 291, the old value `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)` is replaced by a light branch of 70% with the pair reversed, so author links in `.topic-meta-data h5 a` turn much paler on light themes.

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: The light-theme value for group member names changes from 30% to 50% lightness.
reason: In desktop/user.scss line 522, the light branch is 50% where the old value was 30%, so light themes change, while every other line in the PR keeps the old value as the light branch.

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: The mobile custom-message-length colour is reversed: light themes get 30% instead of 70%.
reason: In mobile/modal.scss line 102, the old value was 70% but the light branch is now 30% with the pair reversed, so light themes get much darker text.

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: The mobile topic-map h3 colour changes from 20% to 50% lightness on light themes.
reason: In mobile/topic-post.scss line 182, the light branch is 50% where the old value was 20%, while desktop and the mobile `.number` rule keep the (20%, 80%) pair.

head: d38c4d5f7443223c81529c22470293771baf9f38
title: The mobile light-theme value for group member names changes from 30% to 50% lightness.
reason: In mobile/user.scss line 497, the light branch is 50% where the old value was 30%, the same light-theme regression as in the desktop file.

head: 5b229316ee4c661836ed1161139692a3e8527444
title: Making `.small-action` a flex container stops the button's `float: right` from working.
reason: In small-action.hbs the buttons sit inside `.small-action-desc`, not directly in `.small-action`, so they are not flex items and their `float: right` still applies. The visible bug still happens: `.small-action-desc` is now a flex item with no `flex-grow`, so it shrinks to its content and the floated button lands at the edge of the text box, not at the right edge of the row. Giving `.small-action-

head: ecfa17b5a79dfdc91e7a4d50b42ae78a35d0a293
title: The fallback chain depends on SiteSetting.default_locale, but the translation cache key does not include it.
reason: Cache key at translate_accelerator.rb:72 omits SiteSetting.default_locale, which FallbackLocaleList#[] uses, and no I18n.reload!/cache clearing exists anywhere in the repo, so fallback-resolved strings stay stale after the setting changes.

head: ecfa17b5a79dfdc91e7a4d50b42ae78a35d0a293
title: Fallback locales are only loaded in web requests, and a failed fallback gets cached.
reason: Only application_controller.rb:159 calls I18n.fallbacks.ensure_loaded!; jobs (app/jobs/base.rb:151) only set I18n.locale, and translate loads only config.locale, so :en fallback is not loaded there and the missing result is cached by getset.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: The skipToken path still grants Duplicate, so cloud rules show Duplicate based on Grafana's create permission.
reason: With skipToken, useIsGrafanaPromRuleEditable returns loading:false, so Duplicate becomes toAbility(AlwaysSupported, getRulesPermissions('grafana').create) (useAbilities.ts lines 309/313/318), and canDuplicate ORs it in at AlertRuleMenu line 91 for cloud rules.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: Federated rule groups are no longer treated as immutable by useAllAlertRuleAbilities.
reason: useAllAlertRuleAbilities now calls useAllRulerRuleAbilities, which hardcodes isFederated = false (line 245), dropping the old isFederatedRuleGroup(rule.group) check; RuleActionsButtons.tsx:57 still uses it for Update.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: The list view loses Delete and Pause, and probably Silence, when no ruler rule is passed.
reason: In the prom-only list path Delete needs `rulerRule` (AlertRuleMenu line 165), Pause needs a Grafana ruler rule (line 123), and the silence drawer only opens when rulerRuleType.grafana.alertingRule(rule) is true (V2 line 104), so Silence is shown but opens nothing.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: The `key` prop was dropped from the list item rendered inside `rules.map`.
reason: FilterView.tsx line 157 renders GrafanaRuleListItem inside rules.map without key={key}, while the other branches keep their key.

head: 8df850371034b73dc4dd9908cc30fa09f12a1f97
title: ORing the Prometheus-based abilities can override the ruler's provisioned-rule immutability.
reason: The backend Prometheus API model has `provenance` (prom.go:188) and api_prometheus.go:708 fills it, so the Prometheus path still detects provisioned rules.

head: 303cdc2caf256aa5df660611120c2e3f7392365d
title: TestLogger.FromContext returns a fresh logger, so logs written through it can't be seen.
reason: FromContext returning NewTestLogger() mirrors the existing New() at fake.go:18-19, and a search of pkg/ shows no test that checks InfoLogs on a TestLogger passed to the logger middleware, so nothing fails today and the issue only affects tests that may be written later.

head: 04cfa3bfd469c035ff8b35f9a66867c4e8d5dcf4
title: Debug logging left in at Error level, including every ID in each batch.
reason: Lines 534/537, 554/557, 576/579 log at Error level on every normal batch, including the full ids slice, which is leftover debug logging that will spam error logs.

head: 04cfa3bfd469c035ff8b35f9a66867c4e8d5dcf4
title: All cleanup jobs now run every minute instead of every 10 minutes.
reason: cleanup.go:77 changes the shared ticker to time.Minute*1, which also runs every other job in cleanupJobs (snapshots, dashboard versions, images, invites, short URLs, query history) 10x as often, which the deadlock fix does not need.

head: 04cfa3bfd469c035ff8b35f9a66867c4e8d5dcf4
title: One placeholder per ID can exceed the bind-parameter limit on Postgres and MySQL.
reason: Batch size comes from cleanupjob_batchsize (setting.go:710, MustInt64(100)) with no upper bound, and deleteByIDs lines 615-617 bind one parameter per ID on non-SQLite databases, so values over 65535 exceed the Postgres/MySQL placeholder limit.

head: b1613e320acff00623e6efc59f00ee68c7684a97
title: Cache isn't checked again after taking the write lock, so concurrent cold requests each reload the assets.
reason: After `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` on line 49 the code goes straight to reloading the manifest without checking `entryPointAssetsCache` again, so concurrent cold requests each repeat the load one after another under the exclusive lock, which is real wasted work.

head: 26fed312840cd76b766cbd2158e17a7e6c0ec548
title: The storage-server integration test is now skipped on Postgres instead of being fixed.
reason: Commit 6f4d7087 ('skips postgres integration test. Only fails in drone. Will fix later.') and the TODO comment show the author made this skip on purpose and explained it.

head: 26fed312840cd76b766cbd2158e17a7e6c0ec548
title: The new TotalDocs() call reads the bleve cache map without a lock while indexes can be written into it.
reason: bleveBackend.TotalDocs (bleve.go:144-153) loops over b.cache without cacheMu while BuildIndex writes b.cache[key] (lines 137-139), and the new call at search.go:216 runs after the event goroutine has started.

head: 26fed312840cd76b766cbd2158e17a7e6c0ec548
title: Removing the per-request Init checks also removes the "service is stopping" guard set by Stop.
reason: Stop still sets s.initErr = 'service is stopping', but with every handler's s.Init(ctx) call removed, nothing reads initErr per request, so requests that arrive after Stop are no longer rejected.

head: 1950a511026d520a7329c7b6b9ee60a4af8f8b55
title: V2 now throws UnsupportedOperationException for legacy client operations that worked before.
reason: With ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 enabled, AdminPermissions.management returns MgmtPermissionsV2 (AdminPermissions.java:40-41), so the legacy token exchange check at AbstractTokenExchangeProvider.java:276 now calls ClientPermissionsV2.canExchangeTo, which throws UnsupportedOperationException (line 149) and turns a deny into a 500.

head: 1950a511026d520a7329c7b6b9ee60a4af8f8b55
title: A missing all-clients type resource causes a null dereference.
reason: getResourceTypeResource returns null when the schema is unsupported or the 'Clients' resource is missing (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:117-133), and StoreFactoryCacheSession.findByResource calls resource.getId() right away (line 938), so line 219 throws a NullPointerException with no null check.

head: e944e2acf1e64421860a8e827f93ad06c169621b
title: Cleanup removes an IDP named "alias" instead of the IDPs the test created.
reason: Lines 381/425 register `get("alias")::remove`, so none of the created idp-alias-* providers are removed, and since isImportAfterEachMethod() defaults to false (AbstractKeycloakTest:271) the realm isn't re-imported and the leftovers carry into later tests (the 404 part is wrong, as TestCleanup.addCleanup ignores exceptions).

head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696
title: isAccessTokenId never checks the grant shortcut: wrong offset and inverted condition.
reason: Line 483 uses substring(3,5) (yields 'ta' for 'onrtac') and returns false on equality, so the grant shortcut is never actually verified.

head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696
title: New abstract getShortcut() breaks existing custom grant-type factories and can stop the server from starting.
reason: OAuth2GrantTypeFactory is in server-spi-private (no compatibility guarantee), all in-repo factories implement getShortcut, and returning null violates the documented contract.

head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696
title: The null check meant for rawTokenId checks grantType again.
reason: Line 73 calls requireNonNull(grantType, "Null rawTokenId not allowed"), so rawTokenId is never null-checked.

head: daffb05b5ad091d3ec09933c3c99c2b54f448696
title: The public copy constructor Context(Context) is removed.
reason: A repo-wide search finds no caller of the removed Context(Context) constructor, and it belongs to the private SPI module.

head: 7355f05e6aafe2a7acc6434fb40c686665416606
title: Having `view` permission on groups also passes `canManage()`.
reason: GroupPermissionsV2 line 70 grants canManage() on VIEW or MANAGE, and GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup (line 181) relies only on auth.groups().requireManage(), so a view-only admin can create groups; canManage(GroupModel) and ClientPermissionsV2.canManage() check MANAGE only.

head: 7355f05e6aafe2a7acc6434fb40c686665416606
title: Group-ID filtering uses the authz resource's ID where it needs the group ID (the resource name).
reason: AdminPermissionsSchema creates group resources with name = group.getId() (resourceStore.create(resourceServer, name, ...)), so passing groupResource.getId() to hasPermission/findByName misses, and the returned set holds store-generated resource IDs instead of group IDs.

head: 7355f05e6aafe2a7acc6434fb40c686665416606
title: V2 `groups()` now returns an implementation that throws on V1 permission calls.
reason: Throwing UnsupportedOperationException for V1 management methods is the established V2 design: ClientPermissionsV2 lines 188-195 throw the same way, and the same listener already calls clients().setPermissionsEnabled.

head: 4def149a50c4b9b2c24fbb753ac60fe4f4df0cac
title: The reader thread is never joined, and it spins forever if a delete throws.
reason: `deletedAll.set(true)` (line 155) runs only if every `remove()` in the forEach succeeds, and the reader thread started at line 139 is never kept, joined or made a daemon, so a failed delete leaves it spinning, and the assertion at line 157 can run before an in-flight exception is recorded.

head: 4def149a50c4b9b2c24fbb753ac60fe4f4df0cac
title: `getSubGroupsCount()` can now return null, which moves the NPE to callers that unbox it.
reason: The only caller of `getSubGroupsCount()` is `GroupUtils.populateSubGroupCount` (line 90), which passes the result to `GroupRepresentation.setSubGroupCount(Long subGroupCount)`, a boxed parameter, so null is never unboxed.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: OptimizedCursorPaginator handles the datetime key as a number, so the optimized audit-log path fails.
reason: With order_by='-datetime', line 840 calls math.floor/ceil on a datetime, which raises TypeError, and line 843 returns the raw int cursor; DateTimePaginator (lines 233-241) does the epoch conversion this class lacks.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: Negative cursor offsets are passed to Django queryset slicing, which raises.
reason: Line 880 passes the client-supplied negative cursor.offset straight to queryset[start_offset:stop], and Django querysets raise ValueError on negative indexing, so the request ends in a 500.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: Segments over 1000 spans have their earliest spans dropped silently, with no metric or log.
reason: The commit message for 74618671 says the intent is to evict the oldest spans by end timestamp during insert, so the silent eviction is the intended design and the missing metric is a remark, not a defect.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: `organization_context.member` can be None, which crashes every audit-log request for those callers.
reason: RpcUserOrganizationContext.member is typed `RpcOrganizationMember | None = None` (model.py:346), and line 71 dereferences it on every request whenever the caller is not a superuser, so non-member callers get an AttributeError.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: The shared BasePaginator still slices with negative offsets on prev cursors, and the extra-row check no longer matches the clamped offset.
reason: Negative offsets on prev cursors were already passed to the slice before this change, and the line-192 comparison only runs when is_prev is set, where start_offset equals offset, so the claimed count mismatch cannot happen.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: Redirect depth limit lowered from 10000 to 1000 without a stated reason.
reason: Lowering the loop bound is a scope remark on the authored spans commit; it only matters for segment trees deeper than 1000 levels, and the finding names no concrete failure.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: Switching keys from SET to ZSET breaks on keys that already exist in Redis during rollout.
reason: Keys of the same `span-buf:s:` names are switched from sadd/sscan to zadd/zscan/zcard, so set-typed keys left by the previous version (up to the one-hour redis_ttl) cause WRONGTYPE errors during rollout.

head: 8ab88145113dd23a930e23b9cbbcf8b30e4c0b17
title: A missing `end_timestamp_precise` raises KeyError and stops batch processing.
reason: The payload is cast to the SpanEvent schema type, and the field is used downstream (enrichment.py, message.py) and set in test fixtures (cases.py:1286); the finding itself admits it could not show the field is ever missing.

head: 9501091c52ae94e8d916f79b35d21975b3f9cadb
title: `queued` default is set once at import time, not per instance.
reason: Line 18 `queued: datetime = timezone.now()` is evaluated once when the class is defined, and from_integration never passes queued, so every instance gets the same stale timestamp.

head: 9501091c52ae94e8d916f79b35d21975b3f9cadb
title: Task kwargs now carry a raw `datetime`, which a JSON task serializer cannot encode.
reason: src/sentry/conf/server.py:739 sets CELERY_TASK_SERIALIZER = "pickle" (accept content {"pickle"}), which serializes datetime fine, so the JSON failure cannot happen.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Hidden attributes are only filtered out when a search query is present.
reason: The early `return sorted;` at line 62 skips the HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES filter whenever the search query is empty, so the hidden attributes still show in the default view.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: With the feature flag on, every table widget renders as an empty table.
reason: The commit message says this is part 1 and that the table "is not being used yet"; the empty placeholder sits behind a flag that has not been wired up, which is intentional.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Data migration turned into a no-op that points to a 0921 migration this PR does not add.
reason: src/sentry/migrations/0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py exists in the repository and contains convert_org_saved_searches_to_views.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: The revised migration is also made a no-op, and the 0921 replacement it points to is missing from this PR.
reason: The 0921 replacement migration exists in the repository (0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py:12), so the conversion still runs.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Zipping `error_ids` with `events.values()` assumes nodestore returns every id, in request order.
reason: nodestore base get_multi removes duplicate ids and builds the result from uncached ids first, then adds the cached items (lines 184-205), so values() order can differ from error_ids and zip mislabels events.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Error timestamps (seconds) are compared with breadcrumb timestamps (milliseconds), so errors end up in the wrong place.
reason: Nodestore event timestamps are epoch seconds and rrweb recording event timestamps are epoch milliseconds, so the comparison at lines 153-155 puts every error before the first breadcrumb.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Second placeholder group lost its gap and vertical alignment.
reason: The second placeholder group at line 27 is a bare `<Flex>` without align or gap, while the removed FlexBox gave it align-items:center and gap: space(1); this is a small visual regression.

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Attribute-key lookup stops sending the selected environments
reason: The code says on purpose "environment left out intentionally as it's not supported" (line 50).

head: ea188e2d736fd6ed27c1dba8aae63b7268e2a7a9
title: Attribute-keys query no longer turns off retries or window-focus refetch
reason: DEFAULT_QUERY_CLIENT_CONFIG already disables refetchOnWindowFocus, but it does not set retry, so dropping `retry: false` means a failing request is retried with react-query's default (3 times) before the error shows.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: After the first rebalance, the shared queue pool is shut down and later messages are dropped but still committed.
reason: `create_thread_queue_parallel_worker` (result_consumer.py:247-258) hands the factory's single `self.queue_pool` to every strategy, while `SimpleQueueProcessingStrategy.close()` (line 338) shuts that shared pool down; after a rebalance, `put()` on the shut-down queue raises, and `submit`'s except marks the offset complete without processing it.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: The work queues have no size limit, so there is no backpressure despite the docstring's claim.
reason: `queue.Queue()` at line 185 has no maxsize and `submit` never raises `MessageRejected`, so nothing applies the 'Natural backpressure' the docstring promises (line 253); the queues grow without limit when processing slows.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: The error-handling test asserts the opposite of what the code does and only passes on timing.
reason: The worker's `finally` (line 149) completes offsets 100 and 101 even when processing fails, so the 1s commit loop will commit them, and line 1922's assertion that nothing was committed only holds if it runs before that tick; that makes the test timing-dependent and contradicts its own docstring.

head: 9966ec5a13e331659c3ea00981f9b11b0faf821f
title: The arroyo `Commit` callback is called from a background thread.
reason: `_commit_loop` calls arroyo's `commit` callback from its own daemon thread (lines 270, 287), unlike every other mode in result_consumer.py, which commits through `CommitOffsets` on the consumer thread; arroyo's commit state is not synchronized for that.
